LAYERS, HIDDEN, FFN, VOCAB, KV_HEADS, HE.source: the ONNX graph: MatMulNBits K/N attributes, past_key_values.N.key shape and elem_type, GroupQueryAttention node count
LAYERS, HIDDEN, FFN, VOCAB, KV_HEADS, HE.wrong_when: the model changes -- previously literals, which is why this file would have gone on printing Phi-3.5 numbers for any other model

PEAK_BYTES_PER_S.source: 128-bit GDDR6 @ 16.0 Gbps, published for NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU
PEAK_BYTES_PER_S.wrong_when: the run used a different part -- so the part name is checked against the run's timestamp fingerprint, not assumed

SPEC_PART.wrong_when: a run on another device is quoted against this peak; the check fires

WEIGHT_STREAM_BYTES.source: sum of B and scales initializer sizes over the graph's MatMulNBits nodes
WEIGHT_STREAM_BYTES.wrong_when: the quantisation or the model changes; was a literal restating probe_roofline.py, so the two could drift apart silently

intermediate_breakdown_bytes.source: node counts by op_type from the graph (measured) x a per-node traffic rule (assumed): every tensor crossing a dispatch boundary is written once and read once
intermediate_breakdown_bytes.wrong_when: never, by observation -- nothing here observes activation traffic. It is the size of a prize, not a reading, and must not be quoted as one

kv_bytes().source: LAYERS x 2 x past_len x KV_HEADS x HEAD_DIM x FP16 (all inputs measured)
kv_bytes().wrong_when: never, by observation -- GroupQueryAttention runs on CPU in this EP, so no dispatch of ours reads this cache and no counter of ours sees it

weight_reread_amplification.source: weight_reread_phi35.json, produced by probe_weight_reread.py: a SIMT execution of the compiled SPIR-V located by digest against the proof ledger
weight_reread_amplification.wrong_when: the kernel re-reads a blob, or two workgroups share one -- both are witnessed positive by controls in that probe

device_observed_in_run.reason: timestamp fingerprint period=1.0 bits=64 matches exactly one device

weight_reread_amplification.verdict: each weight byte is named by exactly one load instruction
